figure_fold_illusion.title: Geometric separation of the SBL collapse mechanism and origin of the Fold Illusion. (a) The 3D fast-slow phase space $(e, \Delta\theta, G_0)$ shows the critical manifold $\mathcal{M}_0$ (blue surface) terminating transversally at the physical boundary $e = 0$ without an interior turning point. A genuine thermodynamic fold $\mathcal{C}_{\text{fold}}$ (red curve) occurs only when the slow Surface Energy Balance (SEB) system loses rank ($\det DG_{\text{slow}} = 0$), while normal hyperbolicity ($\lambda_f < 0$; vertical blue vectors) remains intact up to detachment. (b) Projection of $\mathcal{M}_0$ onto the 2D turbulent-stability plane $(\mathrm{Ri}, e)$ creates an apparent turning point (amber dashed curve), producing the illusion of an interior TKE catastrophe. (c) Spectral diagnostics along the trajectory confirm that collapse is driven by slow thermodynamic rank loss ($\det DG_{\text{slow}} = 0$) while fast turbulence attraction ($\lambda_f < 0$) persists throughout.
figure_fold_illusion.label: fig:fold_illusion

figure_gspt_manifold_tikz.title: Geometric Singular Perturbation Theory (GSPT) phase-space schematic illustrating nocturnal transition geometry. The active turbulent branch ($\mathcal{M}_0^+$) forms an upper potential cup in state space. Progressive radiative cooling deforms the cup until the attracting equilibrium disappears at the fold curve $\mathcal{C}_{\text{fold}}$, driving a rapid vertical transition along fast fibers to the weakly turbulent manifold ($\mathcal{M}_0^0$). On this lower branch, ageostrophic inertial adjustment generates the nocturnal low-level jet until accumulated vertical shear triggers turbulent re-ignition.
figure_gspt_manifold_tikz.label: fig:gspt_manifold_tikz
